findings.claim: New CLI option `sharedViteServer` must exist as a key in the user config type that `VitestCLIOptions` is derived from, and must actually be read by the config resolver
findings.rationale: `cliOptionsConfig` is a mapped type over the public config interface, so adding a key that isn't declared in `UserConfig`/`TestProjectInlineConfiguration` will either fail to typecheck or (if the type is loose) silently produce a flag that is parsed into the config object and then ignored at runtime. The hunk only adds the CLI entry - nothing here shows the corresponding config-type declaration or the resolution logic that honors it. Medium confidence; worth verifying both ends exist in this change.

findings.claim: Option documents a default of `true` but provides no `default`/negation metadata, so `--no-shared-vite-server` (the only way to actually turn it off) may not be generated
findings.rationale: The description advertises `(default: true)`, which means the only useful CLI invocation is the negated form. Vitest's CLI builder derives `--no-*` flags for boolean options; if that derivation depends on the entry being recognized as boolean (no `argument`, no `subcommands`), this matches the neighboring `strictTags` entry and is fine. Still worth confirming that `--no-shared-vite-server` is emitted in help output and parses to `false` rather than being rejected as an unknown option. Moderate confidence; consistency with `strictTags` suggests it probably works.

findings.claim: Adding a CLI option without regenerating the generated CLI docs will break the docs-generation check
findings.rationale: This repo generates `docs/guide/cli-generated.md` (and related test snapshots) from `cliOptionsConfig`; adding an entry without re-running the generator typically fails CI. Not a runtime bug, but a concrete consequence of this line. Medium confidence.

findings.claim: A root-only/server-lifecycle option exposed as a plain CLI flag may be silently ignored when set on a project config
findings.rationale: "Let inline projects ... reuse the Vite server of the config that declares them" is inherently a parent/root-level concern. If `sharedViteServer` is only honored on the root config, users setting it inside a project config (or CLI values propagated into project configs) will see no effect and no warning. Other root-only options in this file are usually excluded from project config or validated with an explicit error. Low-to-medium confidence - depends on how the option is resolved.
